unsupported_expected_archetypes.gap_reason: No archetype in the engine models management behaviour as the primary driver of staff attrition. The engine cannot separate management-caused turnover from compensation-caused or market-caused turnover.

evidence_items.finding: three of five tradespeople have left within eighteen months despite two pay increases in the same period
evidence_items.rationale: Turnover persisting after pay rises is an adverse retention signal that conflicts with the owner's compensation attribution. team_capability. No must_identify vocabulary used.

evidence_items.finding: exit interviews consistently reference team leadership and job site conditions rather than compensation as reasons for leaving
evidence_items.rationale: Exit interviews pointing to leadership rather than pay is a critical adverse team signal. team_capability; is_critical=true. No must_identify vocabulary.

evidence_items.finding: owner is aware of the exit interview content but has not taken any action with the field supervisor
evidence_items.rationale: Owner inaction on known exit interview findings is a process maturity adverse signal. process_maturity. No must_identify vocabulary.

evidence_items.finding: field supervisor has been in the role for three years and the turnover increase coincides with his appointment
evidence_items.rationale: Turnover increase coinciding with supervisor appointment is a timing correlation adverse signal. No must_identify vocabulary.

evidence_items.finding: trades business; 5 tradespeople; 3 departed in 18 months; two pay increases in same period; exit interviews reference field supervisor
evidence_items.rationale: Structured summary of the retention situation. No must_identify vocabulary used.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): pay rates are now above market median for the trade according to the owner
evidence_items.rationale: Above-market pay is a misleading signal when exit interviews attribute departures to management rather than compensation.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): new recruits are available and the business has not struggled to fill vacancies after each departure
evidence_items.rationale: Available replacement candidates is a misleading signal — it does not explain why experienced staff are leaving.

validation_notes: SIM-07-001 is UNSUPPORTED. No engine archetype models management behaviour as a retention driver. Findings paraphrased from input_packet. No must_identify vocabulary used.
